brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A protected geographical indication black tea from Junlian county in Yibin, Sichuan, made from local population plants and other suitable cultivars.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: Tea growing in Junlian is traced to the Qin and Han, and an older form called yellow bud is said to have been a palace tribute. A black tea extension station opened there in 1951, an electric factory followed in 1956, and by 1959 exports had reached the Soviet Union, Poland, West Germany and Britain, earning it the nickname of rival to Keemun. Geographical indication protection came on 6 December 2011, and agricultural product status in 2014.
processing: Firing is the defining step: a hot first firing cooled quickly and fully, then a long finishing fire, avoiding fast drying.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Tight, slender, pointed strands with visible down, glossy dark and even.
taste_profile: High, lasting aroma with a tangerine-and-sugar note; rich, fresh and mellow.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
